best_for: Fansubbers, video editors and accessibility teams who fix subtitle timing, translate or transcribe, and want waveform-based editing for free.
description:
Subtitle Edit is a free, open source editor for video subtitles from Nikse, under the MIT license. Version 5 is the cross-platform edition. The project says it collects nothing from your subtitle or media files, and that editing, converting, video playback and auto-backup all run on your own computer.

A Fix Common Errors tool cleans up the usual mistakes, and a separate check flags lines that break Netflix's subtitle rules. You can batch convert files between formats, also from the command line with seconv, strip text meant for hearing-impaired viewers, change the frame rate, merge two subtitle files, or burn subtitles into the video. Styles for Advanced SubStation Alpha and WebVTT can be edited too.

points.title: Time subtitles against the sound
points.text: A waveform and spectrogram view lets you line each subtitle up with the audio. Sync tools shift or stretch timing, and a spell checker catches typos.

points.title: Transcribe, translate and OCR
points.text: It can make subtitles from speech with Whisper, translate them with Google, and turn image subtitles from Blu-ray (SUP) and DVD (VobSub) into text with Tesseract OCR.

points.title: Online services see your text
points.text: Translation, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, OCR and dictionary lookups can use online services. When you pick one, your data goes to that provider.

points.title: Windows needs 22H2
points.text: The Windows build needs Windows 10 version 22H2 (build 19045) or newer with updates installed; older builds can fail with a .NET runtime error. The builds include .NET, so you install nothing else. The installer is 64-bit and installs for all users.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 12
points.text: The Mac disk images, for Intel and Apple Silicon, need macOS 12 or later, with macOS 14 recommended. They bundle libmpv and ffmpeg, and since 5.2.0 they are signed and notarized by Apple.

points.title: Free under MIT
points.text: Subtitle Edit is open source under the MIT license, with no paid tier. The Windows listing keeps 29 versions; macOS lists only the current release. The project also offers Linux builds, which are not listed here.
